title: Developer experience: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site procedures, and top support fixes
author: Maya Patel
summary: Operating playbook and canonical templates for Developer Experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues with canonical fixes. Intended for DevEx contributors, SDK authors, and support engineers.
body:
## Purpose
This page consolidates standards, templates, and canonical content for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the list of top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to make docs consistent, discoverable, and easy to maintain so customers can onboard and integrate with Redwood products quickly.

## Scope
- Applies to all DevEx-owned pages under /eng-developer-experience (sdk-guides, quickstarts-and-templates, docs-site, api-examples).
- Audience: SDK engineers, technical writers, solutions engineers, support on-call, onboarding PMs.

## Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: DevEx documentation team (eng-developer-experience).
- Doc owner: Maya Patel (author).
- Maintainers: SDK owners for language-specific guides; Support for canonical fixes.
- Escalation: if a doc impacts SLAs or product behavior, escalate to the SDK guild lead (see team roster).

## Doc types and when to use them
1. SDK guide (long-form) — full reference + migration notes. Use when the SDK has >1 endpoint or requires lifecycle examples.
2. Quickstart (1-2 pages) — small end-to-end example to get started in <10 minutes.
3. API example snippet — single-file example used across SDKs and the docs site.
4. Template pages — standardized skeletons (see Templates section).
5. Operating procedure — internal docs-site workflows, publishing, and incident docs for the docs site.
6. Top support issues — canonical troubleshooting and fixes for repeat customer problems.

## Templates (canonical skeletons)
Copy these skeletons when creating new pages. Each template is available in the DevEx templates repo.

- SDK guide template (required sections):
  - Title, short description (one line)
  - Compatibility & versions (minimum supported versions)
  - Installation
  - Authentication & configuration
  - Quick usage examples (auth, single-call, streaming)
  - Advanced usage (batching, caching, retries)
  - Migration notes (breaking changes)
  - Troubleshooting & top known issues
  - API reference links
  - Ownership & related pages

- Quickstart template:
  - Title, target audience, prerequisites
  - 10-minute goal (what the user will achieve)
  - Step-by-step instructions (numbered)
  - Minimal code example with copy-paste commands
  - Next steps & links to SDK guide and API reference

- API example snippet guidelines:
  - Keep examples <40 lines where possible
  - Show default error handling and retries
  - Include both minimal and production-ready variants (comments on when to use each)
  - Use consistent request IDs and example payloads across languages

## Quickstarts (recommended set)
- Text completion quickstart (Node, Python, Go) — minimal auth + request + streaming example.
- Chat with function/tool-calling quickstart — server and client snippets.
- Embeddings & similarity quickstart — index, query, rerank flow.
- Private deployment onboarding quickstart — VPC and KMS steps for Private customers.

## SDK guides: structure & best practices
- Use the canonical template above.
- Place language-specific caveats and idioms near the top (e.g., async/await patterns for Node/Python).
- Provide both sync and streaming examples where supported.
- Document default retry/backoff behavior and recommended settings for production (example values below).

Example recommended defaults (display as config table in docs):
| Setting | Recommended value | Reason |
|---------|------------------:|--------|
| retry.max_attempts | 3 | Recover transient 5xx errors |
| timeout.call | 60s | Covers long generation on large context |
| batch.max_tokens | 1024 | Prevents memory blowups on GPU nodes |

## API examples: canonical patterns
- Authentication: show environment variable approach and CLI token injection.
- Idempotency: examples for safe retry (use request_id header).
- Streaming: show both server- and client-side handling patterns.
- Tool calling: include function signature and deterministic examples for model->tool orchestration.

Minimal Node example (copyable):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-large', prompt: 'Translate to French: "Hello"' });
console.log(resp.text);
```

## Docs-site operating procedures (publishing workflow)
1. Author creates draft in the appropriate subspace and applies labels. Use template.
2. Add reviewers and set status = in_review. Reviewer checklist required: correctness, code compiles, security check (see security checklist below).
3. After reviewers approve, set status = published and notify #devex-docs Slack channel.
4. For breaking API changes, coordinate with Product & Release to add deprecation banners and migration assistant.
5. Archive or mark deprecated docs with a deprecation header and link to migration guide.

Reviewer checklist (short):
- Does example compile/run?
- Are dependency versions pinned?
- Are secrets redacted?
- Is the performance/behavior claim accurate?
- Are cross-links added to related pages?

Security checklist (required for SDK/API examples):
- No secrets in examples (tokens, keys).
- Use ephemeral/example tokens only.
- Confirm any network instructions do not expose customer data.

## Top support issues & canonical fixes (current list)
1. Auth failures (401) after SDK upgrade
   - Symptoms: immediate 401 on requests after upgrading SDK.
   - Root cause: SDK changed default auth header name (legacy-token vs authorization).
   - Canonical fix: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and migrate code to client that uses `authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Clear local env caches and restart processes.
   - Example remediation steps (numbered):
     1. Confirm token: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`
     2. Restart app process / container
     3. Upgrade to SDK >= v1.4.2 which normalizes headers

2. Streaming stalls or truncated responses
   - Symptoms: client receives partial stream and then socket closes.
   - Root cause: client-side network timeouts or HTTP proxies buffering chunked responses.
   - Canonical fix: Increase client-side read timeout, disable proxy buffering, or use the SDK's built-in streaming client which sets chunked transfer.
   - Quick fix commands: adjust timeout in environment or SDK config (example: `REDWOOD_STREAM_TIMEOUT=300s`).

3. Embedding mismatch (vectors not matching server output)
   - Symptoms: Similarity queries return unexpected results after model upgrade.
   - Root cause: Model or tokenization change; embeddings model version mismatch between index build and query time.
   - Canonical fix: Rebuild embedding indexes with the new model and add model-version tag to index metadata.

4. High tail latency for small requests in Dedicated
   - Symptoms: p95/p99 spikes despite low throughput.
   - Root cause: batching policy misconfigured, small-request flush thresholds too high.
   - Canonical fix: Adjust batching policy: lower max_batch_wait_ms to 5ms for interactive routes; tune autoscale pool size. See runbook link.

5. Private deployment: unable to connect to control plane
   - Symptoms: Agent can't reach control plane endpoints; customer reports offline nodes.
   - Root cause: VPC routing/NAT or expired control-plane certificate.
   - Canonical fix: Verify outbound rules for control-plane IPs and rotate control-plane certs per upgrade SOP.

## Troubleshooting playbook (how to add new canonical fixes)
1. Triage: support engineer creates a new support ticket and triage note in the regression-triage space.
2. Reproduce: attempt to reproduce with minimal steps and record logs (request_id, timestamps).
3. Root cause analysis: summarize cause, affected versions, and mitigation.
4. Draft canonical fix: add to this doc under Top support issues and file a PR to the quickstarts-and-templates folder.
5. Peer review: have at least one SDK owner and one support owner sign off.
6. Publish and notify customers if release requires action.

## Maintenance and review cadence
- Quarterly content review for all SDK guides and quickstarts.
- Immediate review triggered by: model or breaking API changes, major incidents, or customer-impacting support trends.

## Onboarding checklist for new DevEx contributors
- Read this page and clone the DevEx templates repo.
- Run local docs site: `make site-local` and verify changes render.
- Submit one quick PR updating an existing quickstart (non-production change) for review.
